chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: "NBC" is a slightly infelicitous acronym -- is it "non backwards compatible" or its antonym, "non breaking change"?

chat.author: Ketan Talaulikar
chat.text: it has been expanded on first use :-)

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: I was thinking of the future

chat.author: Ketan Talaulikar
chat.text: Good Q for @Joe and co.

chat.author: Boris Khasanov
chat.text: "non breaking change" - sounds cool!

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: It's a term in common use, and, as noted, has the opposite meaning of "non backwards compatible"...

chat.author: Christian Hopps
chat.text: Heh, how unfortunate

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Naturally backward compatible.

chat.author: Christian Hopps
chat.text: I just asked gemini and claude: "NBC acronym meaning in computer science when discussing changes"

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Naturally broken code

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Huh, at least one reference gives Joe's def'n but not the one I was familiar with. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

chat.author: Christian Hopps
chat.text: Claude mentioned YANG as eample use and said almost certainly means non-backward-compatible. But it's probably been influenced by me. Gemini says the opposite saying Non-Breaking-Change is more common; however, it does specifically list YANG as an example where the other meaning is almost for sure.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: :man_facepalming:

chat.author: Christian Hopps
chat.text: I also saw another summary that said if the context is commits or pull-requests NBC probably means non-breaking change, and if context is APIs or YANG modules NBC probably means not backward compatible haha

chat.author: Christian Hopps
chat.text: so what about commits that affect APIs :)

chat.author: Kesara Rathnayake
chat.text: Authors tools have an experimental pyang checker https://author-tools.ietf.org/yang and plans to add yanglint and pyang formatting support.

chat.author: Joe Clarke
chat.text: NBC is non-backwards-compatible.  It would be a potentially breaking change.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Yeah, I got that, it just makes me ever so slightly sad that not only is the acronym overloaded, it's overloaded to mean two things that are opposites.

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Nearly Backwards Compatible

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: +1 on the thanks. Interesting preso.
